sections.title: Two ways to say not
sections.content: Use *nincs* to say that somebody or something is not in a place: *Károly nincs a konyhában.* Use *nem* to say that something is not what you named: *Ez nem a konyha.* *Nem* stands right before the word it denies. *Nincs* already means “is not there”, so it needs no *van*.

items.english: Károly is not in the kitchen.
The bag is not in the room.

items.spanish: Ez nem a fürdőszoba, ez a hálószoba.
items.english: This is not the bathroom, this is the bedroom.

sections.content: Ask yourself what you are denying. If a person or thing is missing from a place, it is *nincs*. If you are correcting a name (“this is not the kitchen”), it is *nem*. Never write *nincs* and *van* together.
